title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Georgia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Georgia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Georgia: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Following a death in Georgia, medical notification, civil status registration, notarial estate administration, and international document apostille are handled through the Public Service Development Agency (PSDA) and Public Service Halls [5] [6] [8]. We set out the five key administrative steps below so families and representatives can move through mandatory filings without missing Georgia's six-month inheritance acceptance window [2].

steps.title: Secure medical certification and register the death
steps.html:
• Medical certificate of death: Under Article 71 of the Law of Georgia on Civil Status Acts, if death occurs in a medical, pathology, or forensic institution, that institution's head or authorized representative must notify the registration authority within five business days using an electronic medical certificate of death [1] [5]. For deaths outside a medical facility, contact 112 emergency services so police or forensic authorities can examine the scene and confirm identity [9].
  • Who submits and where: Registration of the death of a Georgian citizen, stateless status holder, or any person who died in Georgia is mandatory under Article 70 and is processed at any Public Service Hall (House of Justice), Community Centre, or territorial office of the Public Service Development Agency (PSDA) [1] [5] [8].
  • Required records: Under Article 72, registration relies on the electronic or printed medical death certificate (or a municipal mayor's report or court decision declaring a person deceased), plus the applicant's ID and any foreign passport of the deceased [1] [5] [9].

steps.title: Arrange burial, cremation, or international repatriation
steps.html:
• Local burial rules: Coordinate cemetery permits and municipal burial arrangements using the civil death certificate [9]. Note that commercial cremation facilities are generally unavailable inside Georgia, so families wishing cremation typically arrange transfer abroad [9].
  • Repatriation and police clearance: Where a foreign national's body is repatriated, a local funeral director obtains mortuary embalming and zinc-lining certificates, sanitary clearance, civil death certificates, and any forensic release if a post-mortem was conducted [9].
  • Apostille certification for foreign use: Georgia has been a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention since 14 May 2007 [7]. Request an apostille on the Georgian death certificate and certified translations directly through PSDA or Public Service Hall counters (or repeated civil certificate issuance counters) before sending documents abroad [6] [7].

steps.title: Open the estate with a notary within six months
steps.html:
• Strict six-month acceptance deadline: Under Book Six, Article 1424 of the Civil Code of Georgia, an heir must accept an estate within six months from the day the estate opens (date of death), either in person, by formal acceptance filing, or through an authorized agent [2].
  • Role of Georgian notaries: Under Article 1306 of the Civil Code and the Law of Georgia on Notaries, succession proceeds by will or intestacy through any licensed notary listed by the Notary Chamber of Georgia [2] [3] [10]. The notary checks the electronic inheritance and wills register and issues a certificate of right to inheritance after statutory periods are satisfied [3] [10].
  • Check cross-border documents: If heirs reside abroad, powers of attorney or renunciations executed outside Georgia must be apostilled (or consularly legalized if from a non-Convention state) and translated into Georgian with notarial certification [3] [7].

steps.title: Verify state pensions, social assistance, and bank accounts
steps.html:
• Halt state pensions and inquire about targeted aid: Notify the Social Service Agency (reachable via the Ministry of Health 1505 hotline or Public Service Hall service desks) to stop old-age pension or targeted social allowance payments granted under the Law of Georgia on Social Assistance [4] [8].
  • Recover frozen bank balances: Notify Georgian commercial banks with the official death certificate; bank accounts are normally frozen upon notification until heirs present a notarized certificate of right to inheritance or court order [2] [3].
  • Cancel utilities and property registrations: Update real estate and vehicle entries through the National Agency of Public Registry desks inside Public Service Halls once inheritance certificates are issued [8] [10].

steps.title: Address inheritance tax exemptions and deceased tax arrears
steps.html:
• First and second line heir exemption: Under Article 82 of the Tax Code of Georgia, property received as inheritance or gift by first and second line heirs (children, spouse, parents, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren) during a fiscal year is fully exempt from personal income tax [11]. Third and fourth line heirs enjoy an exemption up to GEL 150,000 per tax year [11].
  • Responsibility for tax arrears: Under the Tax Code, unpaid tax liabilities of the deceased up to the date of death must be settled by heirs proportionally to their share in the inheritance, calculated from receipt of the inheritance certificate, and heirs must notify the Revenue Service upon receiving the estate [11].

contacts.name: Public Service Development Agency (PSDA)
contacts.note: Maintains Georgia's civil status registry, processes death registration and repeated certificates, and serves as primary Apostille Competent Authority.

contacts.name: Public Service Hall (House of Justice)
contacts.note: Front-office branches across Georgia accepting death registration applications, apostille requests, property registry updates, and social filings.

contacts.name: Notary Chamber of Georgia
contacts.note: Official hotline (+995 32 220 67 77) and directory of licensed Georgian notaries administering inheritance files and wills.
